Batch done: 2/2 indexes · 34 IDs dropped at authoring · 0 files still unclean

hoist_to_index: KT-API-01: Explicit API strict mode is on for every published module — explicitApiWarning()/ExplicitApiMode.Warning do not count.

KT-API-03: Exactly one ABI gate runs (standalone BCV by default, abiValidation() where the build already carries the Experimental opt-in), its .api dump is committed, and its check task is wired into `check`. Running neither is the finding. **pinned**
KT-API-04, KT-API-05: In a published Kotlin API, never add a parameter (a default value does not help), never widen or narrow a return type, and never expose a `data class`.
depth.routing_row: | Changing a public Kotlin signature, adding a default parameter, exposing a `data class`, turning on explicit API mode, or wiring BCV / `abiValidation()` | [kotlin-quality/api-and-abi.md](kotlin-quality/api-and-abi.md) |
rule_ids_dropped: KT-API-10: dropped per authoring note 6 (SHOULD with a self-written carve-out, no mechanical check, well-known API-design restatement). Survives as one prose clause in Scope, ID recorded as retired and not reused.

KT-API-11: dropped per authoring note 6 (CONSIDER, reading heuristic, narrow enough that the prose line is cheaper than the row). Survives as one prose clause in Scope, ID recorded as retired and not reused.

depth.routing_row: Launching, awaiting, cancelling, or collecting; anything with `suspend` in the signature
hoist_to_index: KT-CORO-01: set the four detekt coroutine rules `active: true` in the committed config (pinned default) - a `buildUponDefaultConfig` build runs none of them, so a green detekt gate proves nothing about coroutine correctness.
KT-CORO-05: rethrow `CancellationException` from every catch clause wide enough to observe it, `runCatching { }` included - it is a blanket `catch (Throwable)`.
KT-CORO-07: never fix a shared-mutable-state race with `@Volatile` - use an atomic, `Mutex.withLock`, or coarse-grained `withContext` confinement.

rule_ids_dropped: M-V-03: not dropped, folded. The five interop annotations ship as a problem-to-annotation reference table plus one rule row (KT-INTEROP-05) rather than five rows. Five rows would have been five statements of one confusion, and only the @JvmStatic half fails the diff test unaided.
KT-API-07 (@JvmOverloads versus @IntroducedAt binary compatibility): not this family's to define. Cited in Scope and in failure mode 10, owned by KT-API in api-and-abi.md, never restated.

M-V-07 kept at CONSIDER per the map's own adjudication (genuinely split). Its -Xallow-result-return-type half ships as an explicit historical-only correction per wave 4 conflict 13, not as a live gate.
depth.routing_row: Exposing a Kotlin declaration to Java callers, calling Java from Kotlin, writing @JvmStatic / @JvmOverloads / @Throws, or setting a nullability severity flag
hoist_to_index: KT-INTEROP-01: a public declaration whose value comes from a Java call declares its Kotlin type explicitly, and declares it from the Java side's annotation rather than from what the first call site accepted.
KT-INTEROP-02: never lower a nullability severity flag to warn or ignore. JSpecify is strict by default from Kotlin 2.1.0, JSR-305 is warn, so a JSR-305 module sets -Xjsr305=strict explicitly.

KT-INTEROP-07: a published Kotlin module ships a blocking or CompletableFuture-returning wrapper beside every suspend member of its public surface (pinned default, overridden once module-wide by a Kotlin-only adopter).

KT-COMP-04: Set `compilerOptions.jvmTarget` explicitly wherever `jvmToolchain(N)` is set, and equal to the Java side's `options.release` in a mixed module — the toolchain does not move the bytecode target, which still defaults to 1.8.
KT-COMP-08: A new Kotlin module needing an annotation processor uses KSP; a `kapt(...)` line is acceptable only with a comment naming the processor that has no KSP implementation.

KT-COMP-02, KT-COMP-03: Never write `-Xjvm-default` as a string flag, and a library publishing Kotlin interfaces states `compilerOptions.jvmDefault` explicitly — the default flipped to `ENABLE` in Kotlin 2.2.0.
depth.routing_row: Setting `jvmToolchain` or `jvmTarget`, adding a `-X` compiler flag, applying KSP or kapt, or bumping Kotlin, KGP, KSP or Dokka

hoist_to_index: KT-TEST-02: A Kover floor is a `verify { rule { bound } }` block, and `check` already depends on `koverVerify` (0.7.0+) — the finding is an `onCheck = false`, a `disable()` or a `-P` gate, never a missing `dependsOn`.

hoist_to_index: KT-ERR-01: Never wrap code that may throw a JVM `Error` or a test assertion in `runCatching { }` — it catches `Throwable`, and because it is `inline` no detekt rule can ever see it.
KT-ERR-03: `.use { }` every `Closeable`, and never return a `Sequence` or `Flow` built over one — neither type is `AutoCloseable`, so `.use` never reaches it.
depth.routing_row: Catching, wrapping or swallowing a failure; opening anything that must be closed; leaving the process

GRADLE-STRUCT-11: never put an org.gradle.* key in a gradle.properties that is not a build root, it is never read and the team believes it was.
GRADLE-STRUCT-12: gate remote build-cache push on possession of a write credential read through providers.environmentVariable(...).isPresent, never on CI-ness or a branch name.
GRADLE-DEP-18: Never write a dependency version that has not been observed to resolve against the real repository in this session.

depth.routing_row: Declaring a dependency, choosing api/implementation/compileOnly, importing a platform or BOM, resolving a version conflict, locking or verifying dependencies, or bumping a version
